title: Remove timing-fragile tests that turn CI red on slow runners
description: Main CI #174 (44990101974, 341563c) failed on two code checks that passed on re-run: (1) tests/playtest/policy.test.ts 'lineUpPolicyFactory plays the preset at 6 seats…' (TASK-6.6) plays 2×200 six-max line-up hands with a Maniac under coverage: 17.5–20 s normally, 31 s on a slow runner, past the 30 s per-test timeout; (2) e2e/action-bar-limits.spec.ts:33 (TASK-3.7, Chromium) expected seat 5 to act after a fixed 1,000 ms paused-clock budget, but seat 4's bot reply from the advice worker had not arrived — the same worker-vs-clock race class TASK-3.27 fixed in rapid-pace.spec.ts. Such failures stop autopilot. User asked (2026-11-22) for a small fix story that also sweeps for other tests with tight timing margins.

nodes.title: Remove timing-fragile tests that turn CI red on slow runners
Bootstrap the strict TypeScript project with one-command checks
Rank showdown hands by real poker hand rankings
Deal every hand from a seeded shuffle with a replay code
Play a complete fixed-limit hand from blinds to showdown
Give each deciding seat only its own view of the hand
Run seeded bot-only hands from the command line
Run every check in GitHub Actions on each push and pull request
Face TAG bots that act from the advice engine
Vary TAG's play in mixed spots from its style data file
Face a Calling station that calls where TAG would fold or raise
Face a Maniac that bets and raises where TAG would check or call
Face a Rock that folds every hand outside a narrow starting range
Seat bots by line-up preset with unique names
Draw bot randomness only from the replay code and seat
Compute a hand's equity against opponent hands
Recommend a preflop action from the 6-max chart
Recommend call or fold after the flop from equity and pot odds

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given the unit (coverage) test group on CI, When it runs, Then no single test takes more than 10 s on the last green CI run, and the TASK-6.6 lineUpPolicyFactory checks keep their assertions (the 200-hand 6-max comparison moves to the sweep group or the opt-in slow group, with a smaller every-push version kept in unit)

Given e2e/action-bar-limits.spec.ts with a paused clock, When the bot at seat 4 replies late from the advice worker, Then the test still passes because it advances the clock until the expected seat is to act (bounded), instead of a fixed 1,000 ms budget — proven by delaying worker replies in a test run

Given every unit, sweep and e2e test, When per-test durations from the latest main CI run are compared with their timeouts, Then each test that uses more than 50% of its timeout, and each e2e test that advances a paused clock by a fixed budget while waiting for a worker reply, is listed in the story doc and fixed (or justified)
Given the changes, When CI runs on the branch, Then all jobs are green and no test assertion is removed or loosened
